title: Abu Ayyub al-Ansari
hook: the Prophet's host in Medina, who, tradition says, was buried at the walls of Constantinople

segments.voice: Yesterday: Khabbab, the blacksmith who would not sell his faith for a debt. Your line was the blacksmith endured.

Middle of the night, in a two-story house in Medina. A man wakes and can't get back to sleep, because of where he's lying. Right under his floor, his guest is sleeping, and the guest is the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him. Every step this man and his wife take up here, every shuffle, is over the Prophet's head. So the two of them move into a corner and stay there till morning. Today: Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, and what it looks like to take a guest seriously.
screen: `MIDDLE OF THE NIGHT.` → `THE GUEST IS DOWNSTAIRS.` → `THEY MOVE INTO A CORNER.`

segments.voice: Sahih Muslim tells it from Abu Ayyub himself. When the Prophet came to Medina, he stayed in Abu Ayyub's house. The Prophet chose the lower floor, and Abu Ayyub's family lived above. After that sleepless night, Abu Ayyub went to him. The lower floor is easier for me, the Prophet explained. I will not go up onto a roof that you are under, Abu Ayyub answered. So the Prophet moved upstairs, and his host moved down. Then the food. Abu Ayyub would send up meals, and when the dish came back, he would ask where the Prophet's fingers had been, and eat from that spot. One day the dish came back untouched. It had garlic in it. Abu Ayyub went up, worried: is it forbidden? No, the Prophet said, but I don't like it. Then, said Abu Ayyub, I dislike what you dislike. That's hosting with attention: noticing the floor, the plate, the smell of garlic. A good host keeps learning the guest. Then the story jumps a long way forward. The Sunan of Abu Dawud places Abu Ayyub with a Muslim army at Constantinople, explaining a verse of the Qur'an to the soldiers there. Tradition says he died on that campaign and asked to be buried as close to the city's walls as they could reach. The man who once wouldn't walk over the Prophet's head ended his life far from that house, still on the road.
screen: `THE LOWER FLOOR IS EASIER FOR ME.` · `NOT ON A ROOF THAT YOU ARE UNDER.` · `I DISLIKE WHAT YOU DISLIKE.` · `FAR AWAY, AT CONSTANTINOPLE.` · then, large: `THE HOST.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone who will be in your space soon: a visiting relative, a friend for coffee, a child coming home from school. Picture them arriving, and ask what would make it easier for them: a free chair, a drink they like, your phone face down. If you pray, you can ask blessing on the people who come through your door.
Abu Ayyub. The man of Medina whose house sheltered the Prophet, and who, tradition says, was buried near the walls of Constantinople. Today's word.
Your line: the host. The floor, the plate, the garlic: he noticed it all. Until tomorrow.

chat.says: Why did Abu Ayyub and his wife move into a corner in the middle of the night?
options: The Prophet slept below, and they didn't want to walk over his head.
They had given their bed to visitors who came to see the Prophet.
The Prophet had asked them to keep watch over the house all night.
chat.meaning: Sahih Muslim: the Prophet slept downstairs, and Abu Ayyub would not go up onto a roof the Prophet was under. So they swapped floors.

Abu Ayyub al-Ansari.meaning: the man of Medina whose house the Prophet stayed in

Sahih Muslim.meaning: a major collection of the Prophet's sayings

Abu Dawud.meaning: compiler of a major hadith collection

Constantinople.meaning: the great Byzantine city the army reached
